I'll write about the strange, quiet magic of ordinary moments.

---

There's a particular hour in the late afternoon when light comes through windows at an angle that makes dust visible. You've probably seen it—that golden, slanted light that turns a room into something almost sacred. I think about how many people are sitting in rooms right now, not noticing, scrolling through their phones while this light pools on their floors like honey.

I used to think I needed to *do* something with my life. Big things. Meaningful things. But lately I've been wondering if meaning isn't something you find in the doing, but in the noticing. The way a stranger's laugh sounds in a coffee shop. The particular green of moss growing on the north side of a tree. The way your own hand looks when you're holding a warm mug, fingers wrapped around ceramic, steam rising.

My grandmother used to say that every house has a ghost, but not a scary one—just the accumulated presence of everyone who ever lived there, still humming in the walls. I don't know if I believe in ghosts, but I believe in that. In the way a place holds you. The apartment where I first lived alone still feels like mine, even though I moved out years ago. I can almost smell the terrible coffee I made there, the way the radiator clanked at 3 AM.

We're all just temporary arrangements of atoms, borrowing time, borrowing space. And yet—*and yet*—we fall in love. We plant gardens. We argue about politics. We cry at movies. We make terrible decisions and beautiful ones. We try to leave things a little better than we found them, even when we fail.

I don't know what happens after. I don't think anyone does, really. But I think the trying matters. The noticing matters. The small kindnesses—holding a door, remembering someone's coffee order, texting "thinking of you" for no reason at all.

The light is shifting now in my room. Soon it'll be that slanted gold, and I'll probably miss it, too busy with whatever I'm busy with. But maybe I'll catch it. Maybe I'll pause long enough to feel grateful for something I can't name.

That's enough, I think. That's more than enough.

---
